then.text: The warden sent word. The chapel looks lovely, apparently. That's the best report I'll get all year.
The Chief at the Marina Boathouse has the whitewash. Then East Point, and the warden. Be respectful, won't you.

else.text: Welcome. I'm the Staff Officer for Naval Party 1002. We run the Territory's affairs on the spot, with a small team and a lot of paperwork.

The history of these islands isn't a comfortable one. Between 1967 and 1973 the Chagossian people were removed, mostly to Mauritius and Seychelles, and many have been fighting to return ever since. We don't pretend otherwise.
There's a heritage visit coming, and the chapel and cemetery at East Point want tidying. Would you collect whitewash and brushes from the Chief at the Marina, and take them to the Heritage Warden?

then.text: My grandmother's island is out there somewhere past the lagoon. I'm going to sit and look at it for a bit.

else.text: {greeting} I'm here on a heritage visit. My grandmother was born on Peros Banhos. I was born in Crawley. Life is strange.
Britain split Chagos from Mauritius in 1965 to make this Territory, and Mauritius became independent in 1968. Between 1967 and 1973 all of our people were sent away.
Mauritius has always claimed the islands. In 2019 the International Court of Justice said Britain should end its administration here. Britain said that opinion wasn't binding.
In October 2024 the two governments announced a deal in principle: sovereignty to Mauritius, with the base on Diego Garcia staying.
Some of us want to come home, some want a say, some trust Mauritius and some don't. What we all want is to be asked. That's not much, is it?
Noted in the Gazetteer, under How these isles work.
